title: Newton's first law of motion (নিউটনের প্রথম গতি সূত্র)
placement: Book page 64, topic 3.1: জড়তা এবং বলের ধারণা: নিউটনের প্রথম গতি সূত্র. Next to the boxed law and the paragraph after it.
description: Newton's first law (নিউটনের প্রথম সূত্র, page 64, 3.1) as a thought experiment the student runs: a vivid red flat-contact laboratory slider with a yellow carrying handle waits on a launcher whose spring is always squeezed to the same red notch, so one tap gives the same push every time (the slider leaves at 3 m/s) onto the floor chosen in a row of words: a jute mat, a wooden floor, ice, or an imagined floor with no friction. The panel is one action, one result, one rule: a big numbered button ("১ ব্লকটিকে ধাক্কা দাও") whose same numbered badge rings the slider on the 3D view (a tap on either pushes), one result line ("মাদুরে ব্লকটি ১.৩১ মি গিয়ে থামল") and one rule that grows with what the student has found, from "বল প্রয়োগ না করলে স্থির বস্তু স্থির থাকে" through friction and a comparison of floors to the slider's first law word for word. Without a push it stays at rest. With friction it slows evenly and stops (1.31 m, 2.55 m, 9.18 m); the view then pulls back down the lane, where a dashed line labelled with each floor shows every stop at once, and the button offers the next floor. With no friction the velocity stays 3.00 m/s, the dots it leaves every 0.05 s stay evenly spaced, and it never stops. Arrows show the velocity, friction against it, and the push only while the paddle touches the slider. Test tab: 5 questions on clean scenes (what a pushed book does with no friction, which force acts while a slider slows to a stop, predicting the ice or the mat from the other floors, which way a slider goes when a curved wall ends, and stopping a gliding book or a slider at rest on a frictionless floor). Phone-first, Bangla.
